sectionTooltips.attachedAssets: ERC-721 and ERC-20 assets attached to gestures, viewable for all cycles or only the current Performance Cycle.
sectionTooltips.gestureTypeDistribution: Share of gestures made with ETH, Random Walk (ETH-paid), and CST over time, sampled at a chosen interval. Current cycle only.
sectionTooltips.enduranceTimeline: A Gantt of who held the lead during a cycle. Each bar is a lead stint (its width = how long that address held the lead). The widest bar is the Endurance Champion; the Chrono-Warrior is the participant whose single continuous reign as Endurance Champion lasted the longest. Pick any cycle to compare.
sectionTooltips.cstWindow: How the CST Calibration Window evolved during a cycle. Every ETH gesture shortens the window slightly; every CST gesture lengthens it. The window sets how fast the CST gesture cost decays to free. Pick any cycle to compare.
sectionTooltips.cstCost: What each CST gesture actually cost during a cycle, on a log scale, alongside the allocation clock remaining right before it. Mid-cycle gestures are often nearly free; in the endgame, rapid gesturing leaves the cost no time to descend and prices can reach thousands of CST.
sectionTooltips.attachedTokenDistribution: Contracts and token counts for ERC-721 assets attached to gestures.
sectionTooltips.cosmicSignatureTokenDistribution: Current owner distribution for Cosmic Signature NFT ERC-721 tokens.
sectionTooltips.cstBalanceDistribution: Current wallet distribution for CST ERC-20 balances.
sectionTooltips.cstTotalSupply: Historical CST ERC-20 supply changes, including imprints and consumption over time.
sectionTooltips.cycleActivations: System event windows that show when protocol cycles or modes became active and ended.
sectionTooltips.uniqueParticipants: Wallets with at least one indexed gesture, sorted by gesture count.
sectionTooltips.uniqueRecipients: Wallets that received indexed protocol allocations.
sectionTooltips.uniqueEthContributors: Wallets that contributed ETH to the protocol.
sectionTooltips.anchorReleaseActions: Chronological anchor and release actions for the selected NFT type.
sectionTooltips.anchoredTokens: Tokens currently anchored in the selected anchoring wallet.
sectionTooltips.uniqueAnchorHolders: Wallets that have anchored or released the selected NFT type.
sectionTooltips.gestureFrequency: Indexed gesture counts grouped over time to show protocol activity patterns.
sectionTooltips.gestureSpikes: Periods where gesture activity changed quickly compared with surrounding activity.
sectionTooltips.participantActivePeriods: The longest indexed active participation windows for the most active wallets.

anchoringTooltips.cstActiveAnchorHolders: Wallets currently anchoring at least one Cosmic Signature NFT.
anchoringTooltips.cstAnchorDistributionDeposits: Total deposit events into the Cosmic Signature NFT Anchor Distribution pool.

anchoringTooltips.cstUnretrievedAnchorDistributions: Anchor Distributions allocated but not yet retrieved by Cosmic Signature NFT anchor-holders.

endurance.description: Each bar is a lead stint: an address holding the lead from one gesture until the next gesture arrives. Bar width is how long the lead was held. Outlined bars set a new endurance record at the time. The Endurance Champion has the longest single stint; the Chrono-Warrior held the Endurance Champion title longest overall. The legend shows their colors.

cstWindow.summaryFinal: The window was {current} at finalization. During the cycle it ranged from {low} to {high}.
cstWindow.description: The CST Calibration Window sets how long a CST gesture's cost takes to descend from its starting value to free. Every ETH gesture shortens the window slightly; every CST gesture lengthens it. Each dot is a gesture, colored by type; the line is the window in effect after it.
cstWindow.empty: No per-gesture Calibration Window data for this cycle. Cycles indexed before the V2 events do not include it.

cstCost.clickHint: Click the dot to open the transaction.
cstCost.description: Each dot is the CST actually paid for a gesture (log scale — hollow dots were free). After every CST gesture the cost resets near twice the paid amount and descends to free across the Calibration Window. The dashed line shows the allocation clock remaining right before each gesture: when the clock runs low, rapid gesturing leaves the cost no time to descend, so paid prices escalate. Click a dot to open its transaction.
